145	// =========================================================================
146	//  Swizzle mode (PTX ISA §<ip>.4, descriptor bits 62-61 "swizzle mode").
147	//
148	//  The shared-memory matrix descriptor encodes how the 128-bit core-matrix
149	//  rows are interleaved in smem to avoid bank conflicts on the wgmma read.
150	//  CRITICAL: the descriptor's layout_type field (bits 63:62) does NOT use a
151	//  size-ascending encoding. The hardware/CUTLASS encoding is
152	//  (cute/arch/mma_sm90_desc.hpp LayoutType, verified):
153	//    NONE/INTERLEAVE = 0,  SWIZZLE_128B = 1,  SWIZZLE_64B = 2,  SWIZZLE_32B = 3.
154	//  (An earlier draft had 32B=1/128B=3 swapped; the correctness path uses NONE=0
155	//  so it was unaffected, but the perf-phase swizzle modes MUST use these values.)
156	//
157	//  CORRECTNESS-PATH NOTE (deviation flagged in the report): the gated /
158	//  tested numerics path ships swizzle = NONE (kSwizzleNone). NONE is a
159	//  fully-legal descriptor mode (§<ip>.4) and is the layout the
160	//  correctness gates validate against torch. The 128B-swizzle layout is a
161	//  PERF-PHASE optimization (bank-conflict elimination on the smem read) and
162	//  is exposed here as the template parameter the model headers will select
163	//  once the quiet-GPU perf phase measures it; it is NOT required for any
164	//  correctness gate. See DESIGN §4.1 ("specify the 128-byte-swizzle layout"
165	//  is the perf target; phase-1 staging uses cp.async, §4.1 item 3).
166	// =========================================================================
167	enum SwizzleMode : uint32_t {
168	    kSwizzleNone = 0,   // INTERLEAVE / no swizzle (the correctness-path layout)
169	    kSwizzle128B = 1,   // SWIZZLE_128B
170	    kSwizzle64B  = 2,   // SWIZZLE_64B
171	    kSwizzle32B  = 3,   // SWIZZLE_32B
172	};
173	
174	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
175	//  generic-smem-pointer → matrix-descriptor start address.
176	//  PTX ISA §<ip>.4: the descriptor's bits 13-0 hold the start address of
177	//  the matrix in shared memory, encoded as the 18-bit smem byte address with
178	//  the low 4 bits dropped — i.e. addr_field = (smem_byte_addr & 0x3FFFF) >> 4.
179	//  The low 4 bits MUST be zero (16-byte alignment) or they are silently lost.
180	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
181	__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t smem_desc_encode_addr(const void* smem_ptr) {
182	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
183	    uint32_t a = static_cast<uint32_t>(__cvta_generic_to_shared(smem_ptr));
184	    return (a & 0x3FFFFu) >> 4;
185	#else
186	    (void)smem_ptr;
187	    return 0u;
188	#endif
189	}

191	// =========================================================================
192	//  Shared-memory matrix descriptor (PTX ISA §<ip>.4).
193	//
194	//  64-bit layout (bit ranges per the ISA table):
195	//    bits  13: 0  start address (smem byte addr >> 4)
196	//    bits  15:14  (reserved / 0)
197	//    bits  29:16  leading-dimension byte offset (LBO) >> 4
198	//    bits  31:30  (reserved / 0)
199	//    bits  45:32  stride-dimension byte offset (SBO) >> 4
200	//    bits  48:46  (reserved / 0)
201	//    bits  51:49  matrix base offset (for swizzle; 0 for our tiles)
202	//    bits  61:52  (reserved / 0)
203	//    bits  63:62  swizzle / layout mode (0 none / 1 128B / 2 64B / 3 32B —
204	//                 the CUTLASS LayoutType encoding, see SwizzleMode above)
205	//
206	//  LBO and SBO are the byte offsets between consecutive "core matrices" along
207	//  the leading and stride dimensions respectively (§<ip>.3 "Strides").
208	//  Both are encoded >>4 (16-byte granular). The exact (LBO,SBO) depend on the
209	//  operand's smem tile layout; the make_desc_*_kmajor builders below compute
210	//  them for the canonical row-major-K bf16 tiles the model headers stage.
211	// =========================================================================
212	struct SmemDesc {
213	    uint64_t desc;
214	};

216	// Low-level builder: caller supplies LBO/SBO in BYTES; we apply the >>4 and
217	// the swizzle field. Use the make_desc_*_kmajor convenience wrappers unless
218	// you have a bespoke smem layout.
219	template <SwizzleMode Swizzle = kSwizzleNone>
220	__device__ __forceinline__ SmemDesc make_smem_desc(
221	    const void* smem_base, uint32_t lbo_bytes, uint32_t sbo_bytes,
222	    uint32_t base_offset = 0u
223	) {
224	    SmemDesc d;
225	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
226	    uint64_t addr = static_cast<uint64_t>(smem_desc_encode_addr(smem_base));
227	    uint64_t lbo  = static_cast<uint64_t>((lbo_bytes >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);
228	    uint64_t sbo  = static_cast<uint64_t>((sbo_bytes >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);
229	    uint64_t bo   = static_cast<uint64_t>(base_offset & 0x7u);
230	    uint64_t sw   = static_cast<uint64_t>(Swizzle & 0x3u);
231	    d.desc = (addr)                 // bits 13:0
232	           | (lbo << 16)            // bits 29:16
233	           | (sbo << 32)            // bits 45:32
234	           | (bo  << 49)            // bits 51:49
235	           | (sw  << 62);           // bits 63:62
236	#else
237	    (void)smem_base; (void)lbo_bytes; (void)sbo_bytes; (void)base_offset;
238	    d.desc = 0;
239	#endif
240	    return d;
241	}

244	//  Canonical descriptor builders for the bf16 K-major (K=16) smem operand
245	//  tiles the model headers stage (DESIGN §4.3: A tile 64×16 bf16, B tile
246	//  N×16 bf16). Major-K means the contraction dimension K is the operand's

248	//  D[m,n] = Σ_k A[m,k]·B[n,k] with BOTH operands K-major (TransA=TransB=0).

250	//  REQUIRED smem layout (the CUTLASS-canonical Major-K INTERLEAVE layout —
251	//  ground truth, NOT a plain row-major block; see the report's "deviation"
252	//  section). For an operand of MN rows × 16 K-cols of bf16, element (mn,k) is
253	//  at the bf16 index:
254	//      idx(mn,k) = (k/8)*(MN*8) + mn*8 + (k%8)
255	//  i.e. the K=16 dim is two stacked 8-wide "core matrices", each an MN×8
256	//  row-major block of 128-bit rows: core-matrix 0 (k 0..7) occupies the first
257	//  MN*8 bf16 (MN*16 bytes), core-matrix 1 (k 8..15) the next MN*16 bytes.
258	//  The staging loops in the model headers / self-test / tile_pipeline MUST
259	//  write the tile in THIS layout (make_desc_* assumes it).
260	//
261	//  Descriptor LBO/SBO for this canonical no-swizzle (INTERLEAVE) layout,
262	//  derived from cute::make_gmma_desc<Major::K> and verified against the cute
263	//  Layout_K_INTER_Atom byte offsets (report §"descriptor"):
264	//      SBO (stride byte offset)  = 128                 (8 MN-rows × 16 B/row)
265	//      LBO (leading byte offset) = MN * 16             (one core-matrix block)
266	//  Both are passed in BYTES; make_smem_desc applies the mandated >>4.
267	//  make_smem_desc routes lbo_bytes→leading-offset field (bits 29:16) and
268	//  sbo_bytes→stride-offset field (bits 45:32), matching cute's assignment
269	//  (leading_byte_offset_ = stride_10 = MN*16, stride_byte_offset_ = 128).

272	// A operand (LHS), shape M×K(=16) bf16 in the canonical Major-K smem layout.
273	// `MN` is the operand's MN extent (= the wgmma M = 64 for the A tile).
274	template <int MN, SwizzleMode Swizzle = kSwizzleNone>
275	__device__ __forceinline__ SmemDesc make_desc_A_kmajor(const void* smem_base) {
276	    const uint32_t lbo = (uint32_t)MN * 16u;   // one core-matrix block (bytes)
277	    const uint32_t sbo = 128u;                 // 8 MN-rows × 16 B/row
278	    return make_smem_desc<Swizzle>(smem_base, lbo, sbo);
279	}

282	// `MN` is the operand's MN extent (= the wgmma N for the B tile).
283	template <int MN, SwizzleMode Swizzle = kSwizzleNone>
284	__device__ __forceinline__ SmemDesc make_desc_B_kmajor(const void* smem_base) {
285	    const uint32_t lbo = (uint32_t)MN * 16u;
286	    const uint32_t sbo = 128u;
287	    return make_smem_desc<Swizzle>(smem_base, lbo, sbo);
288	}

291	//  fp32 accumulator fragment for an m64×N output tile.
292	//  PTX ISA §<ip>.3 "Register fragment for .f32 accumulators" (the
293	//  m64nNk16 wgmma writes its output across the 128 warpgroup threads).
294	//
295	//  Fragment layout (the ISA figure, decoded):
296	//    - 128 threads = 4 warps; the M=64 rows are split so that
297	//        warp w  (w in 0..3)  owns rows  [16*w .. 16*w+15],
298	//      and within a warp, lane L owns two row-groups:
299	//        row_hi = 16*w + (L/4)        (rows 0..7 of the warp's block)
300	//        row_lo = row_hi + 8          (rows 8..15)

337	//   group_of_8 = i / 8 ;   within = i % 8
338	//   row = 16*warp + (lane/4) + 8*(within / 4)
339	//   col = (lane%4)*2 + (within % 2) + 8*group_of_8 + ...

343	__device__ __forceinline__ void wgmma_frag_decode(
344	    int tid_in_wg, int i, int N, int& row, int& col
345	) {

347	    const int lane = tid_in_wg & 31;       // 0..31

349	    // per thread (8 rows split into 2 row-halves × ... ). The ISA's .f32
350	    // fragment for an n8 slab gives, per lane:
351	    //   reg 0 -> (row = lane/4,       col = (lane%4)*2 + 0)
352	    //   reg 1 -> (row = lane/4,       col = (lane%4)*2 + 1)
353	    //   reg 2 -> (row = lane/4 + 8,   col = (lane%4)*2 + 0)
354	    //   reg 3 -> (row = lane/4 + 8,   col = (lane%4)*2 + 1)

357	    const int slab   = i >> 2;             // which n8 column slab (0..N/8-1)

359	    const int row_half = within >> 1;      // 0 -> rows 0..7, 1 -> rows 8..15
360	    const int col_par  = within & 1;       // 0 or 1 column within the pair
361	    row = 16 * warp + (lane >> 2) + 8 * row_half;

All arch PTX guarded on `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900`; pre-sm_90/gfx942 compile to a documented scalar fallback no-op so the codegen matrix still builds (lines 24-26, 565-591).

### 1.1 Tunables / atom constants (lines 133-143)
- `SG_TUNED_TILE_N` default 128, `SG_TUNED_TILE_M` default 128 (`#ifndef`-guarded so untuned/out-of-tree lift composes — CONTRACT rule 3).
- `kWgmmaAtomM = 64` (FIXED by ISA m64nNk16), `kWgmmaAtomK = 16` (bf16 atom K).

### 1.2 Swizzle enum (lines 167-172) — CUTLASS LayoutType encoding
`kSwizzleNone=0, kSwizzle128B=1, kSwizzle64B=2, kSwizzle32B=3`. Header explicitly flags (lines 152-155) that this is NON-size-ascending (matches cute/arch/mma_sm90_desc.hpp LayoutType) and that an earlier draft had 32B/128B swapped. **Correctness path ships `kSwizzleNone`** (lines 157-165): NONE is fully legal, is what the gates validate against torch, and 128B-swizzle is a deferred perf-phase optimization (no GPU here). Verified against the actual production callers below — all use `kSwizzleNone`.

### 1.3 Address encode (lines 181-189)
`smem_desc_encode_addr`: `(__cvta_generic_to_shared(ptr) & 0x3FFFF) >> 4` → 14-bit field. PTX ISA §<ip>.4. **VERIFIED**: for max H100 optin smem (~227 KB) the field = 14528 ≤ 0x3FFF, fits bits 13:0. Low-4-bits-must-be-zero (16B align) requirement documented lines 104-108, 178-179.

### 1.4 Descriptor packing `make_smem_desc<Swizzle>` (lines 219-241) — VERIFIED no field overlap
64-bit layout (lines 194-204) and the actual packing (lines 231-235):
- addr → bits 13:0
- `(lbo_bytes>>4) & 0x3FFF` → bits 29:16
- `(sbo_bytes>>4) & 0x3FFF` → bits 45:32
- `(base_offset & 0x7)` → bits 51:49
- `(Swizzle & 0x3)` → bits 63:62

I checked all field pairs for bit overlap programmatically: **NO OVERLAP**, each field fits its documented range. The mandated `>>4` (16-byte granular) is applied by the helper; callers pass LBO/SBO in BYTES.

### 1.5 Canonical descriptor builders (lines 274-288)
`make_desc_A_kmajor<MN, Swizzle>` and `make_desc_B_kmajor<MN, Swizzle>` both set `lbo = MN*16` bytes (one core-matrix block) and `sbo = 128` bytes (8 MN-rows × 16 B/row). Derived from `cute::make_gmma_desc<Major::K>` / Layout_K_INTER_Atom (lines 261-269). **VERIFIED** the field values: A MN=64 → lbo_field=64, sbo_field=8; B N=128 → lbo_field=128, sbo_field=8.

Required smem operand layout (lines 250-259, the CUTLASS-canonical Major-K INTERLEAVE, NOT plain row-major): `idx(mn,k) = (k/8)*(MN*8) + mn*8 + (k%8)` — K=16 = two stacked 8-wide core matrices. The selftest's `kmajor_idx` (wgmma_selftest.cu:53-55) is byte-identical to this formula, and the production model_stage headers reference it (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:561, model_stage_vit_tc.cuh:339). This is a load-bearing staging contract: the staging loops MUST write this exact layout or the descriptor reads the wrong matrix.

### 1.6 Accumulator fragment `WgmmaAccum<N>` (lines 314-324)
`static_assert(N%8==0)`, `kRegs = N/2` fp32 regs in registers (NOT smem), `.zero()` clears all. One object per consumer thread; 128 warpgroup threads together hold the 64×N tile (PTX ISA §<ip>.3).

### 1.7 Fragment decode `wgmma_frag_decode` (lines 343-364) — SINGLE source of truth
Decodes `(tid_in_wg, i) → (row, col)`:
- `warp = tid>>5`, `lane = tid&31`
- `slab = i>>2` (which n8 column slab), `within = i&3`
- `row_half = within>>1`, `col_par = within&1`
- `row = 16*warp + (lane>>2) + 8*row_half`
- `col = (lane&3)*2 + col_par + 8*slab`

Note an apparent doc/code drift: the big comment block lines 326-342 sketches a different ("group_of_8 = i/8") factoring than the actual implementation (slab = i>>2). The IMPLEMENTED form (lines 358-362) is the authoritative one and is what the A=I gate validates. The same decode is used by both the epilogue store and the gate reference (wgmma_selftest.cu:116-119) — one source of truth, no chance of mismatched private decode. Per-slab register mapping documented lines 348-356.

### 1.8 Choreography primitives (PTX ISA cites in-file)
- `wgmma_fence()` (lines 374-378): `"wgmma.fence.sync.aligned;"` §<ip>.2.
- `wgmma_commit_group()` (lines 385-389): `"wgmma.commit_group.sync.aligned;"` §<ip>.5.
- `wgmma_wait_group<N>()` (lines 398-403): `"wgmma.wait_group.sync.aligned %0;" :: "n"(N)` §<ip>.6. Compile-time immediate.

### 1.9 The ss-wgmma issues `wgmma_issue_nXX` (lines 442-561) — per-shape explicit overloads
Mnemonic `wgmma.mma_async.sync.aligned.m64nNk16.f32.bf16.bf16` for N ∈ {8,16,32,64,96,128}. Each lists exactly N/2 `"+f"` accumulator regs, two `"l"` (u64) descriptors, then immediates `%scaleD, 1, 1, %transA, %transB` — i.e. **scaleA=scaleB hard-fixed to +1 (no operand negate)** (lines 434-437, the literal `1, 1` in every asm string). PTX ISA §<ip>.1. The `.aligned` qualifier requires all 128 warpgroup threads to issue uniformly with no divergence (documented lines 110-112, 423-425). N=96 is kept because DESIGN §3.1 lists m64n96k16 even though V=99 pads to N=128 in the head GEMM (note lines 503-506).

I verified the operand/immediate `%`-numbering for n8/n16/n32/n64/n96/n128: each correctly numbers N/2 acc regs + descA + descB + scaleD + transA + transB (e.g. n128 uses %0..%63 acc, %64 descA, %65 descB, %66 scaleD, %67 transA, %68 transB — matches the literal asm at lines 537-560).

### 1.10 Dispatcher `wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N,ScaleD,TransA,TransB>` (lines 573-591)
`static_assert` N ∈ {8,16,32,64,96,128}; `if constexpr` chain to the right overload; pre-sm_90 = no-op. ScaleD=0 OVERWRITES (D=A·B), ScaleD=1 ACCUMULATES (D+=A·B).

### 1.11 Mainloop helper `wgmma_mainloop_kchain<N,TransA,TransB,FenceBeforeFirst=true,DescGen>` (lines 617-644)
The full choreography in one call (DESIGN §3.1 determinism rule):
- optional `wgmma_fence()` (default true);
- k=0 issue with ScaleD=0 (overwrite — fresh tile needs no pre-zero);
- `#pragma unroll 1` loop k=1..k_steps-1 with ScaleD=1 (accumulate);
- `wgmma_commit_group()` then `wgmma_wait_group<0>()`.
FIXED ASCENDING k-order (one CTA owns the tile end-to-end, no work-steal split, no float atomics → bitwise reproducible). `gen(k) -> {descA,descB}` callback decouples staging (cp.async vs pre-loaded) so the SAME mainloop is bit-identical pipelined vs unpipelined (gate (c)). FenceBeforeFirst=false documented for the accumulate-onto-existing case (lines 610-615).

## 2. `mma.cuh` — the CUTLASS Sm90 collective (TMA + WGMMA, host-launched). **NOT on the production path.**

Namespace `sg::sm90::mma`. Entire file is `#ifdef WITH_CUTLASS ... #else #error ... #endif` (lines 21, 873-877). Renamed from `csrc/kernels/cuda/_cutlass_gemm.cuh` (line 11). Includes cutlass/cute headers (lines 29-45). Pulls in project headers platform.h/types.h/affine2x2.h/utils.cuh (lines 5-8).

### 2.1 What it provides
- `sm90_get_workspace(bytes)` (lines 68-81): per-thread lazily grown grow-only CUTLASS workspace, process-lifetime, cudaMalloc/cudaFree on grow.
- **Shape-keyed operator cache** (lines 156-367): `GemmCacheKey{M,N,K,A,B,C}` (pointers ARE part of the key because a Hopper TMA tensor map encodes the global BASE ADDRESS — lines 105-117, the load-bearing address-stability safety invariant). FNV-1a hash (lines 170-184), 16-slot direct-mapped `thread_local` cache `Sm90GemmCache<Gemm>` (lines 191-213), eviction frees the entry-OWNED workspace (lines 267-272). The mutex was intentionally dropped (thread_local, single-thread-per-stream launcher) (lines 134-143, 238).
- `sm90_run_gemm_cached` (lines 224-305) and typed-output `sm90_run_gemm_cached_out` (lines 315-367): MISS path builds make_cute_packed_stride + Arguments + can_implement + get_workspace_size + initialize (the cuTensorMapEncode path) + run + install; HIT path just `e.op.run(stream)` reusing baked params_/TMA descriptors.
- Collective builders, all TileShape `128×128×64`, ClusterShape `1×1×1`, FP32 accumulate, `KernelScheduleAuto` + `EpilogueScheduleAuto`:
  - `Sm90Gemm<ElementInput>` (lines 369-445), FP32 output, row-major A/B/C → `sm90_run_gemm` (lines 448-467).
  - `Sm90GemmBT<ElementInput,LayoutBT>` (lines 485-531) → `sm90_run_gemm_bt` (lines 535-553): RowMajor-B = C=A·B, ColumnMajor-B = C=A·Bᵀ.
  - `Sm90GemmBTOut<ElementInput,ElementOut,LayoutBT>` (lines 571-617) → `sm90_run_gemm_bt_out` (lines 622-635): typed output, no FP32 scratch + cast.
  - `Sm90GemmAT<ElementInput>` (lines 655-701) → `sm90_run_gemm_atb` (lines 705-718): ColumnMajor-A = C=Aᵀ·B, for ViT wgrad (half/bf16 only).
- TF32 path: `sm90_run_gemm_tf32` (lines 791-803), `sm90_run_gemm_tf32_bt<LayoutBT>` (lines 808-821), `gemm_tf32` (lines 824-830) — reinterpret_cast `float*`→`tfloat32_t*`, 10-bit mantissa, explicitly flagged 🟡 NOT bit-identical to scalar FP32 (lines 776-780); exact-FP32 callers force scalar via `SG_FORCE_SCALAR_FP32`.
- Convenience: `gemm_fp16` (lines 745-751), `gemm_bf16` (lines 756-762).
- SG2 dt_proj fused: `softplus_bias_kernel` (lines 833-845, 64-bit linear index to avoid INT_MAX overflow, col stays int), `launch_softplus_bias` (lines 847-856, no-op if bias==null), `dt_proj_fused_with_bias` (lines 859-869, gemm_fp16 then softplus+bias).

### 2.2 Two DOCUMENT-STOPs and one REVERT recorded in-file (design rationale, not dead code)
- §8 (lines 384-396): no small-M tile variant (second tile = 2nd slot table + M-dispatch + 2nd full build → nvcc OOM; correctness identical).
- §7 (lines 414-426): no KernelTmaWarpSpecializedCooperative large-M path (needs cooperative epilogue + 2-warpgroup tile + 2nd build; unmeasured win, no GPU).
- TF32 A-transposed REVERTED (lines 720-740): `Sm90GemmAT<tfloat32_t>` fails a CUTLASS HARD static_assert "SmemLayoutB K must be 128bytes to be transposed" (sm90_mma_tma_gmma_rs_warpspecialized.hpp:193) — TF32 4B with 128×128×64 doesn't satisfy it. CONSEQUENCE: ViT wgrad float path keeps scalar fallback; `vit_run_gemm_atb<float>` returns cudaErrorNotSupported.

## 4. POSSIBLE BUGS / RISKS

1. **STALE doc comment (TransB) in wgmma.cuh lines 416-421** — the comment claims "the canonical setting is TransA=0, TransB=1 ... B is N×K which the MMA wants as K×N so it reads B transposed." This CONTRADICTS every actual production caller and the selftest, all of which pass **TransA=0, TransB=0** with both operands in Major-K INTERLEAVE layout:
   - tile_pipeline.cuh:335-339 ("Both operands Major-K ⇒ TransA=0, TransB=0")
   - model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:759-760 (`<N,0,0,0>`)
   - model_stage_vit_tc.cuh:470-472 (`<N,0,0,0>`)
   - wgmma_selftest.cu:111 (`wgmma_mainloop_kchain<N,0,0>`)
   NOT a code bug (the function is fully parametric and the production path passes 0,0), but a misleading comment that could lead a future caller astray. Flag for doc fix.

2. **Doc/impl drift in the frag-decode comment (wgmma.cuh lines 326-342 vs impl 343-364)** — the prose sketches a "group_of_8 = i/8" factoring with an unfinished "+ ..." that does NOT match the implemented `slab=i>>2` form. The IMPLEMENTED form is correct/authoritative (validated by the A=I gate via the shared decode), but the comment is partly hand-wavy/incomplete. Cosmetic/doc risk only.

3. **`make_smem_desc` addr field not explicitly masked to 14 bits (wgmma.cuh:226, 231)** — `addr` is `(byte&0x3FFFF)>>4` (≤14528 for 227KB smem) and OR'd at bit 0 with no `&0x3FFF`. Safe for all realistic H100 smem offsets (verified 14528 < 16383), but if a future arch had >256KB smem-per-block this could collide into bits 14-15 (documented "reserved/0"). Currently NOT a bug; latent assumption worth noting.

4. **mma.cuh `sm90_get_workspace` is dead-but-by-design** (lines 68-81) — it is defined but the cache path (lines 274-282) deliberately uses entry-OWNED workspaces instead, and the comment (lines 119-127) notes the 1×1×1 cluster kGemm path reports workspace size 0. So `sm90_get_workspace` is effectively unused in the only code paths present. Since mma.cuh as a whole is unwired, this is moot, but within-file it is an unused helper.
